headline: PHYSICS WALK — he balances for real now
lede: A 12-mass rigid-body biped lives at /retrogames/demos/physicswalk.html: gravity, joint motors and friction, nothing posed. Tap to push him — light taps stumble and recover, hard ones topple him dead, and the telemetry shows the balancing as it happens.

notes.text: #1204 shipped via PR #1217: the dynamics rung under STICK WALK (IK) — XPBD physics, momentum-conserving joint torques, real heel-to-toe roll.
physicswalkcheck: 28 gates incl. ragdoll honesty, stance-slip <0.35 m/s, GRF-in-stance ≈ body weight, and a balance mutant that proves the harness can fail.

Two physics rewrites to find stability: unclosed torque couples pump momentum (he launched himself 8 m/s), and glue-friction kills foot roll — the fix was penalty contact bounded by the true normal force.
Balance gains are searched, not derived: 60k randomized candidates in Node; the sweep script doubles as the calibration tool.

look.text: Push him around — see the support margin go red before he falls
Compare: the IK twin at the other rung of the ladder
